en: An inclined plane like a ramp reduces the effort force needed to lift a heavy box by increasing the distance over which the force is applied.
Applying rubber treads to bicycle tires increases friction with the road, preventing the wheels from slipping when a rider brakes suddenly.
Earth's gravity pulls a dropped apple downward because the planet's massive center of mass exerts an attractive force on the fruit's smaller mass.
Wrapping an insulated copper wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a battery creates a magnetic field that picks up paperclips.
Rubbing a balloon against human hair transfers electrons to the balloon, giving it a negative charge that attracts neutral pieces of paper.
When white light passes through a glass prism, it refracts and separates into a rainbow because different colors bend at slightly different angles.
Plucking a thick guitar string produces a lower pitch than a thin string because the thicker mass vibrates more slowly through the air.
A metal spoon placed in hot soup becomes warm at the handle because fast-moving soup molecules transfer kinetic energy to the spoon's slower molecules.
Releasing a stretched rubber band converts its stored elastic potential energy into kinetic energy, causing the band to snap forward rapidly.
A seesaw acts as a first-class lever where pushing down on one end applies an upward force to lift a heavy friend on the opposite end.
Boiling water circulates heat through convection because the heated water at the bottom becomes less dense and rises while cooler water sinks.
A wooden block casts a dark shadow on a wall because its opaque surface completely blocks the straight-traveling light rays from a flashlight.
